nodes.text: The Editing Suite
Monitors. The last frame of the film is frozen on screen: Faust's back at the easel, brush up, the canvas still blank.
THE DIRECTOR is at the console. THE WRITER sits on the arm of the couch with a notebook. THE HUMAN BEING is on the floor with his back against the couch, eating holiday fudge out of the foil.
THE ARTIST is at the window, looking out at nothing in particular.
Silence.
Well. That's where it cuts.
That's not an ending.
It's a shot. It's a good shot. Back to camera, blank canvas, morning light. Audiences love a back to camera.
They'll want to know if he got the girl.
He got two friends and a third of a painting and a coffee date with someone he hasn't called in years.
That's not the girl.
That's better than the girl.
(from the window) There wasn't one girl. That was the point. Depends who's looking.
Can we at least get the father and the daughter. One shot. Reunion. Swell the strings. I've got strings.
She doesn't arrive yet.
When does she arrive.
Later. Much later. Somewhere else.
(throwing up his hands) That's not a release date that's a prophecy.
Most of the good ones are.
THE FOOL bursts in through the door, disheveled, carrying a bucket of popcorn that is mostly empty, wearing a t-shirt with a painted wooden frame on it and nothing inside.
Did I miss it. Did they make it. Did the boat come back.
Boat came back.
And the cat?
(gently) Cat crossed.
(sitting down hard) Good. Good. She was tired.
It isn't finished.

(pointing at each in turn) Of course it's not finished, you said so on page one, you said I'm starting something I should never finish and then you were surprised when you didn't finish it. That's like being surprised your teeth fall out in the dream, where your teeth fall out.
I said it has to be completed.
Completed's not finished. Completed is you went all the way there and you came all the way back and you brought something. Finished is you put it in a frame, so it can't leave.
(turning from the window, quietly) Then leave the frame empty.
They all look at the Fool's shirt.
(looking down at it) Oh. Oh, I've got the empty one. Who gave me this.
Nobody answers.
(after a moment, to the Writer) So what do I tell them. The ones who came for an ending.
(closing his notebook) Tell them it's in production.
Tell them thank you. Tell them thank the sun and moon and stars.
Tell them to paint something.
Tell them it's four in the morning and they're awake, so that counts.
THE DIRECTOR looks at the frozen frame a long time. He doesn't hit play. He doesn't hit stop. He leaves it there.
Fine. Roll credits over the back to camera.
What's the last card.
THE FOOL takes a fistful of popcorn, considers the screen, and says it like it's obvious, like it's what anyone would say.
fly not fall.

THE DIRECTOR types it. On the monitor, over Faust's back, over the blank canvas, small and lowercase:
fly not fall.
The suite goes dark, all but the monitor.
